cognitive-development-conservation.alt: Top: two equal glasses of water; one is poured into a tall, thin glass and the child is asked which has more. A typical 4-year-old says the tall one has more, focusing on height alone. A typical 8-year-old says they are the same because the water was only poured. Bottom: Piaget’s four stages with typical ages: sensorimotor, birth to about 2 (object permanence); preoperational, about 2 to 7 (make-believe, egocentrism); concrete operational, about 7 to 11 (conservation, logic about real things); formal operational, about 12 and up (abstract, hypothetical thinking). Later research finds the skills often appear earlier.
